newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline ease on weaker crude, healthy supply.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline ease on weaker crude, healthy supply.

text.p: NWE gasoline eased slightly on Friday as crude prices and perceptions of healthy supply pressured the market in the short-term, traders said.
Summer spec Eurograde barges were last reported traded at $214 fob ARA, having fetched $216 earlier. A winter grade cargo traded at $211.50 in early trade.
April swaps traded at $215.50 fob ARA and were talked at $214 later.
Players attributed some of the weakness to lower crude. They also noted some ARA refineries were keen to off-load winter spec material to clear storage space for summer spec.
"Prompt supplies are fairly healthy," said one. "There's a fair bit of winter spec still available which could put some pressure on."
In the medium-term, most traders remained bullish saying any weakness in the market was unlikely to extend past Easter.
"From where I'm sitting it doesn't look to bad," said another trade. "It's looking pretty balanced and the arb's about to open up. I would expect ARA to mop up available material."
Some traders said that the intentions of a persistant buyer in the market were also causing some concern.

"Some of it was destined for the East and there was even talk that some of it went to the Med but I think they've still got some material left and it will be interesting to see what they do with that," said one trader.
